label: MiniMax M3.1 Flash
output:
Good news first, and then the bit I've been putting off writing.

Priya Bhatia starts with us on Monday 16 November. She's a chartered engineer (IStructE) with nine years at a consultancy in Coventry, and she's the reason our turnaround is about to change. If you see a new face on site, please say hello — she'll be doing a good share of the visits and, frankly, a good share of the talking, which suits her much better than it suits me.

Now the honest part.

For the last two months, our beam calculations and drawings have been taking five to six weeks. That's too long. Several of you waited far longer than you should have, a few of you were quite unhappy, and one review was sharp enough that I still think about it. The slow weeks were my fault. I said yes to too much work on my own, and in October I was out on site visits in the day and still doing calculations until midnight. My wife started calling the office "the other house", and she wasn't joking.

One couple in Harborne had their builder stood waiting with the steel already ordered. We got the calculations to them in three days, but only after they chased us twice. That wasn't good enough, and I'm sorry.

So here's what's changing from Monday. Our target for beam calculations and drawings is ten working days, from the point we have everything we need from you — which I'll always tell you at the outset. Priya joining is what makes that realistic rather than just hopeful.

One other change, and this one affects January. The free first site visit is ending. From 1 January 2027, a first site visit costs £95, and that £95 comes straight off your fee if you go ahead with the job. Any visit already booked when this post goes up stays free, whatever date it's on. I liked offering the free visit, but around a third of them never turned into a job, and charging even a modest amount keeps the visits I do worth doing properly.

If you're waiting on something at the moment, it is moving. Message me directly and I'll tell you exactly where it stands.

Right, that's enough about me. Say hello to Priya when she comes to site — by Christmas she'll know more about load paths than I ever have.
